searchText: This point is super important as it is a potential conflict with BALs <@402853454126776320> did an [analysis on this](https://hackmd.io/@bFEBbZiVSAO0IURh9qzEFg/BJmFYqCeGl) <@429719902363058177> , <@425274498732916736> , <@1252939266871263294> , <@628018527470616606> - can we get your view on this? I can change the EIP accordingly tomorrow if you all agree FYI: <@755913785620824175> > there's a problem with charging CALL in the child frame breaks stipend transfers, transfer() to a fresh account can never cover 183.6k from 2300 gas. It's raised by <@1126229231572094976> This PR is also related for completeness: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/2900 Looks like this point makes the entire proposal meaningless 🥲 . Namely we must pre-frame charge the account creation and refund after-frame if necessary. > a) relocate the account-creation state gas into the child frame I've already given my opinion as well, basically: CALL and CREATE have different behaviours right now regarding accessing the said account (for creation or not), shouldn't we distinguish both cases? I think we should charge the create at the same time we are trying to load the account. Basically my thinking is what's the rationale for changing the current behaviour? - CALL: we need to get the code for the account for what to run in the frame. Doesn't make sense to charge the child for its account creation (this will decrease the gas stipend in the child) - CREATE: don't need the account access until we are in the initcode frame. Which is fine cause initcode frames have boundless gas. It actually matters as CREATE returns 0 if unsuccessful. If you move the OOG check before getting into CREATE you are essentially OOGing the caller so this changes behaviour.

excerpts.author: lu_pinto
excerpts.content:
> a) relocate the account-creation state gas into the child frame
I've already given my opinion as well, basically:

CALL and CREATE have different behaviours right now regarding accessing the said account (for creation or not), shouldn't we distinguish both cases? I think we should charge the create at the same time we are trying to load the account. Basically my thinking is what's the rationale for changing the current behaviour?

- CALL: we need to get the code for the account for what to run in the frame. Doesn't make sense to charge the child for its account creation (this will decrease the gas stipend in the child)
- CREATE: don't need the account access until we are in the initcode frame. Which is fine cause initcode frames have boundless gas. It actually matters as CREATE returns 0 if unsuccessful. If you move the OOG check before getting into CREATE you are essentially OOGing the caller so this changes behaviour.
